function: Excluded, above_phy: the DRL (NsHQPN) learns only the UAV flight speed and the scheduling of ground nodes (p. 7, p. 9), not a physical-layer decision.
notes: Reason above_phy. p. 7: the DRL action space "contains the flight velocity v of the UAV and the service scheduling" of the ground nodes (GNs). p. 9: the actor outputs "each GN corresponds to the speed of one UAV" and the critic outputs "the optimal action in the discrete action space" (the GN to serve); no network outputs a RIS phase, beam, or power. p. 4: "P is the fixed transmission power of the UAV". p. 10: the RIS phase is not learned, "RIS can calculate the optimal phase shift"; Algorithm 3 step 10 only "Configure the phase shift of RIS" (p. 9). The trajectory comes from a convex-hull plus ellipse-fitting algorithm (MICH, pp. 5-6), also not learned. The system does contain a reflecting RIS (10x10 units, Table II, p. 9), but the learning acts on UAV trajectory/speed and GN scheduling, which the instructions list as above the physical layer. Paper reports energy-efficiency results (Table III, p. 12), so the results criterion is not the reason.
